rows.what the ink shows: A thick horizontal cap joins two descending uprights, the right one ending in a small foot. Additional diagonal and curved strokes cross the interior without erasing the product-shaped frame.

The punctuation position immediately after typed Paula is covered by a broad, angular handwritten terminal stroke. No separate dot of an exclamation mark or descending typed comma tail can be isolated under that overprint.

The short first group has a split s stroke and a low connected ending; the second begins with a long descending p and continues through a dipped middle stroke to a crossed t and extended low ending. A small stain obscures part of the middle of projecteur.

The typewritten sequence visibly reads B-r-e-i-f, followed by a letter with one rounded arch and a right upright. That final n has neither the short shoulder of r nor the two arches of m; the following comma is separate.

The final letter is a tall l with a short right-curving foot; a clear white gap separates it from the round following period. The targeted enlargement shows no intervening e, while the preceding dotted i positions and low m/n bodies support minimal.

After T there is a dotted initial i, an extended low joined body with a short d rise, and a distinct final upright with a leftward cross stroke. These strokes support induit despite the compressed middle letters.

Across the deletion, peuvent retains its initial descending p and raised terminal stroke; plonger has another p descent and a separate deep g loop. The following dans begins with an ascender, and the last word has the low linked u-n-e contour.
The crossed-out fragment starts with an upright and a rounded lower cup compatible with U. A dense oval and crossing return cover the short remainder, preventing a reliable separation of n and e.

Above and through the deletion remain the initial descending q form, a tall l-like rise, and a later q descent before the extended final connected group. The middle is partly covered by the horizontal strike, but these separated features support quelconque.

The insertion separates into four groups, beginning with a shallow descending p and then the accented, tall-stroked être. The long third group starts with an open c and has internal dotted/accented rises; a separate low final group supports comme rather than the single nécessairement ending of the alternative.

After d'une and the looped g/ascenders of algèbre, the insertion has a narrow de, a short low von group, and a conspicuous capital N with an extended joined ending. Those last groups differ from the proposed sans atomes, which would lack that capital N.
A separate low n-on group precedes atomique; the latter has a crossed tall t, an i dot, and the deep q downstroke before the terminal low letters.
The initial descending p and a later tall loop survive, but the long cancellation merges the central letter bodies. These remnants do not securely establish the full proposed phrase.
The word begins with a dotted i, then a low n connection and a raised d; a second i dot appears before the short terminal t stroke.
Several raised loops and a final upward connection remain above the heavy horizontal cancellation. The middle bodies and crossings needed to establish exactement are merged into that line.
The compressed initial hooks lead into a tall l loop, a separately dotted i, and the raised t; low terminal strokes end in the hooked s before the comma.

The cancellation preserves an initial small upright, a middle arch and a high terminal looped stroke, while covering nearly all the connecting bodies. The terminal stroke is not securely separable from the cancellation, so bornées remains unconfirmed.
A dot and a small late ascender survive above the deletion, with low humps at the beginning. The heavy bar joins the rest of the letters and obscures the proposed word division.
After the opening parenthesis, the uncancelled word has a short initial s turn, connected low u strokes and an extended terminal r before a separate comma.
The capital has a pointed high apex, oblique left stroke and crossbar, with an open lower swash rather than two stacked B bowls. A separate small 2 sits below and to its right.
The deleted word begins with a closed low bowl and tall d ascender. The following low bodies are joined by the cancellation, preventing a secure reading of ans.

The first word has the tall looped d and a separate terminal s; l and its apostrophe are distinct at the next word. The following a and adjacent d/h ascenders lead into the compressed accented middle and long final connection.
The inserted word has a low onset rising to a tall angular l, followed by a compressed low ors run; it sits above the insertion curve.

The main glyph has two upright shoulders joined across a dark center and a long left descending stroke, supporting a fraktur H rather than a rounded mu. The small lower-right A has a sloping left leg, bowed right leg and crossbar.

After la there is a short doubled horizontal glyph, too compressed to resolve the proposed même confidently. The last word has a tall crossed f, a separate i dot and a low terminal run, unlike the proposed pour.
The initial open C is followed by a long low run with an i dot, then a looped d and an accented low continuation ending in short ons strokes.
The character is pointed and triangular, with a crossbar and a hooked lower-left foot; it has the angular outline of A rather than a rounded theta.
A short low une precedes a separate r onset and extended low run. The latter has a prominent crossed t, a following i dot and a small lifted terminal on stroke.

A hooked f with a long descender survives, together with small rises at the right end. Two heavy deletion strokes cover the central letters, so formes remains plausible but not securely distinguishable.
The first word has a looped e and n hump with no q descender. The next has a descending initial q, a medial crossed t and following i dot, supporting en question rather than que continuons.
The word begins with a tall f whose cross-stroke extends rightward, followed by a separate i dot and a compressed low nies run.

The short second group has a distinct upright l and flattened a tail, supporting la rather than un; the terminal sur remains visible. The first word’s final hook may absorb an e, while the following long horizontal runs do not distinguish théorème/théorie or encore/connue securely.
The beginning is a sequence of low a/n/a strokes before a tall l. The trailing rounded and descending strokes continue to the page corner and support ogue.
